title: Fractional-window-meter-rounding causes cross-scope double-charge under shard merge
creator: Nina Patel
description: Production reports and internal sampling indicate a class of billing/quotas misaccounting that manifests when per-route and per-org meters are merged during shard reconciliation. Small fractional token debits (sub-token charges from streaming/partial responses and attachments) are being rounded independently in multiple aggregators, and a shard merge path can cause those round-ups to be applied twice, producing transient over-billing and incorrect throttles for affected keys.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Create org-level quota (50 tokens/min) and route-level quota (20 tokens/min) for a test tenant.
2) Send a burst of requests that produce fractional debits (e.g., streaming fragments that charge 0.4 tokens each) to the same route across two edge shards.
3) Force a shard rebalance / migration (simulate by moving lease ownership or triggering controlled failover).
4) Observe meter snapshots after reconciliation, and compare summed debits to expected arithmetic sum.
5) Repeat with different fragment sizes and with both prefix caching and KV cache enabled to exercise merge code paths.
observed_behavior: After shard merge, some keys show debit totals larger than the sum of individual shards. Affected customers see overage throttles and billing records with duplicated fractional roundup amounts. Spike duration ranges from 10s to 2m depending on reconciliation timing.
expected_behavior: Decimal/fractional debits must be preserved deterministically across shard compaction and merges; final billed debit should equal the exact arithmetic sum (within unit micro-token tolerance) and not contain duplicated rounding artifacts.

investigation_notes: 2025-02-12: Pager triggered by customer SLOs; initial triage showed correlated edge shard migrations across a small subset of tenants.

2025-02-13: Replayed production trace in staging with deterministic shard handoff; reproduced duplicate-rounding behaviour when per-route aggregator and per-org aggregator both applied independent rounding before persistence.

2025-02-14: Code review of meter merge reveals two levels of granularity: route-level accumulator stored with millitoken precision, org-level compaction converts to centitoken for storage, then merge code re-applies a rounding step causing roundup amplification.
root_cause: Independent rounding semantics in distinct accumulator layers combined with a non-idempotent merge path. Specifically: (a) route accumulator rounds sub-token amounts to N-digit precision when flushing, (b) org aggregator performs another rounding during compaction, and (c) the merge routine treats rounded deltas as additive units rather than reconciling raw micro-token streams. When shards are reconciled, those double-rounded deltas sum to a higher value than the true raw consumption.
mitigation: Short-term: Roll out a server-side reconciliation patch that detects suspicious delta amplification on merge and applies a compensating correction (delta-clamp) for affected keys. Deployed to eu-west-1 only to limit blast radius.
Mid-term: Backfill billing correction script to refund confirmed overcharges for tenants with repeated amplification events.
Long-term: Normalize all accumulators to a canonical micro-token unit and adopt monotonic-idempotent merge semantics plus deterministic rounding at the final billing write step only.
proposed_fix: A. Change internal accumulator units to microtokens (integer arithmetic) across route/org/global layers to avoid floating rounding divergence.
B. Update merge algorithm to operate on raw microtoken deltas and perform a single deterministic rounding only at the storage/billing boundary.
C. Add merge-time checksums and idempotency tokens to detect duplicate-applies from replayed events.
D. Add property-based tests and a synthetic reconciliation harness that simulates concurrent shard flushes with randomized fractional events.
E. Add observability: a reconciliation anomaly metric (reconciled_delta - expected_delta) and an alert if > 0.1% of traffic exhibits amplification.
rollout_plan: 1) Land microtoken changes behind feature flag and enable in staging. (2d)
2) Run deterministic reconciliation harness against existing persisted snapshots to validate no net drift. (3d)
3) Canary deploy to 5% of shards in eu-west-1 with anomaly monitoring. (2d)
4) Expand to 25% and run billing backfill checks. (3d)
5) Global rollout after 10 days of stable metrics and manual QA signoff. (continuous)
Rollback: feature-flag off and run compensating agent to normalize any mid-rollover inconsistencies.
qa_plan: Unit tests for microtoken arithmetic and merge idempotency.
Property tests that fuzz fractional event orderings and verify final sums match reference big-rational implementation.
Staging replay of 48h production trace and differential comparison against current runtime.
Manual spot-check of billing records and confirm refund pipeline for sample tenants.
